DRAG DROP -
Refer to the exhibit. Drag and drop each traffic flow type from the left onto the corresponding number on the right. Not all traffic flow types are used.
imageNote: Diagram: WAN router - Internet/DCI, two spine switches, two leaf switches under DC1, connected to Web Server, App Server, Storage Node 1, Storage Node 2. Numbered arrows 1 (WAN router to spines, orange), 2 (leaf to Web Server, magenta), 3 (leaf to App Server / storage, red), 4 (leaf to Storage Node 2, green), 5 (spines to DCI, blue).
theory: Data center traffic is commonly classified by direction and purpose: north-south traffic moves between clients outside the DC and servers inside it; east-west traffic moves server-to-server within the DC (common with distributed/multi-tier apps); storage traffic runs between hosts and storage arrays; storage replication runs array-to-array; and inter-data-center traffic crosses a DCI link between separate sites. "North-west" and "south-west" are not real traffic-classification terms and are included only as distractors that should not be matched. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 4 — Data Center Traffic Patterns)
